newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan says HK fortunes under Beijing irrelevant.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan says HK fortunes under Beijing irrelevant.

text.p: Whether Hong Kong flourishes or fails under communist China's rule makes no difference to Taiwan in its bitter rivalry with Beijing, Foreign Minister John Chang said on Thursday.

Though the estranged Republic of China on Taiwan will watch Hong Kong closely after it reverts to Beijing rule on July 1 and wishes the territory well, the handover carries no lessons for Taiwan, Chang said.
"We will benefit if Hong Kong stays stable," Chang told Reuters Television in an interview.
"But if Hong Kong stays stable, it does not mean that the so-called one-state, two systems formula can be sold to us, can be applicable to us. Nobody believes that," he said.

Taipei has repeatedly scorned what Beijing maintains is a generous offer -- political, economic and even military autonomy under a "one country, two systems" model in exchange for recognising the communist state's sovereignty.
Chang said mishandling of Hong Kong would raise questions about the communist leadership's competence and erode confidence in Hong Kong and Macau, which reverts to China in 1999.
But Nationalist-ruled Taiwan, estranged from the mainland since a 1949 civil war split, will persevere, he said.
"We will still choose our own way for our own future. It has nothing to do with the success or failure of one state, two systems," he said. "We don't think it will have anything to do with us."
Taiwan's cabinet on Thursday adopted detailed regulations under a law governing the island's future ties with Hong Kong and Macau. The rules take effect from July 1.
Vice President Lien Chan, who doubles as cabinet chief or premier, was quoted by state media as saying the rules showed Taiwan's desire to maintain close ties with Hong Kong.
"I hope the Chinese communists can live up to their promise to the people of Hong Kong -- letting Hong Kong people rule Hong Kong so that Hong Kong can maintain its prosperity," Lien said.
Chang suggested China was hurting the unification cause by squeezing Taiwan diplomatically and menacing it militarily, as with its huge 1995-96 war games and missile tests near Taiwan.

"(If) the R.O.C. is truly destroyed or totally isolated by mainland China, some people very naturally will think that we will have to find a way to create a new state, to have a breakthrough into the international arena," he said.

Chang scoffed at mainland President Jiang Zemin's March offer to name a Taiwanese as his vice president, saying all of China should unite under democracy and leave the people to choose their leaders at the ballot box.
"If we can be (elected) president, why should we take the vice presidency? Chang mused.
"When the whole of China is unified under a democratic system, people may choose our people to be president. Maybe they will get rid of Jiang Zemin and some other people if it is a true democracy.
"It is under such a system that we hope that China can be reunified," Chang said.
He said Taiwan already was a flourishing, sovereign democracy with the means to defend itself and would not allow its future to be negotiated in private the way Hong Kong's was.
"We are totally different from Hong Kong, socially, politically, militarily," Chang said.
"We have our own armed forces to defend ourselves. We have our own system that was achieved through our own efforts. Our future definitely shall not be negotiated with mainland China."
As for the likely success of Hong Kong's transition, Chang expressed personal doubts but said few people wished it ill.
"I think that most people, 90 percent of people on Taiwan will hope that Hong Kong will be all right. The rest, the 10 percent, are crazy people," he said.

"But I would not be sincere if I told you I felt very comfortable about the future of Hong Kong after July 1 because so far mainland China has made some mistakes, according to my personal view, over Hong Kong.
"Maybe Hong Kong will be all right over the first two or three years. But when it goes beyond the year 2000 I have no grounds to say it will be the same. I hope it will be the same.
